title: MatterGen generates TaCr2O6; SIAT synthesizes a disordered version with bulk modulus 169 GPa against a 200 GPa target
summary: Microsoft's diffusion model generated a structure conditioned on bulk modulus 200 GPa; SIAT (Shenzhen) synthesized it and measured 169 GPa, with Ta/Cr compositional disorder. Vendor co-authored proof.
account: Zeni et al. (Nature, 16 January 2025) are Microsoft Research AI for Science with co-authors including the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology. They present MatterGen, a diffusion model over 3D crystal geometry trained on about 608,000 stable materials. Its outputs are reported as more than twice as likely to be new and stable as those of earlier generative models. As a proof of concept they synthesized one generated structure and measured its property “within 20% of our target”. Microsoft's blog identifies the compound as TaCr2O6, generated for a bulk modulus of 200 GPa. Prof Li Wenjie's SIAT group measured 169 GPa. The structure matched MatterGen's proposal “with the caveat of compositional disorder between Ta and Cr”. The synthesis is vendor co-authored, and a Nature news critique of 1 October 2025 was paywalled beyond its lede. That critique is not among the sources, and no independent experimental replication was found.

headline: Microsoft's MatterGen generates TaCr2O6, measured at 169 GPa
metric: a bulk modulus of 200 GPa and measured at 169 GPa

comparator.against: previous generative models for crystal structures (DiffCSP, CDVAE and others) on the same benchmark
comparator.before: not stated as a figure in the text (previous generative models)
comparator.after: more than twice as likely to be SUN (stable, unique and new); the synthesized TaCr2O6 measured at 169 GPa against a 200 GPa design target
comparator.quote: Combining both model and data improvements, MatterGen generates structures that are more than twice as likely to be SUN compared with previous generative models, whereas the generated structures are up to an order of magnitude closer to their local energy minimum.

later.note: A Materials Horizons paper by Mikkel Juelsholt (12 June 2026) reports that the synthesized disordered TaCr2O6 is identical to Ta1/2Cr1/2O2, a compound first described in 1971 and included in MatterGen's training dataset, so the proof-of-concept material was not new.
later.quote: However, detailed crystallographic analysis presented in this paper reveals that this is not a novel compound but is identical to the previously reported Ta1/2Cr1/2O2, first described in 1971 and included in MatterGen's training dataset.
